hook.text: JFK's advisors unanimously backed the Bay of Pigs invasion. Everyone agreed and nobody questioned. It was a disaster.

buildup.text: Janis coined groupthink: cohesive groups suppress dissent to maintain harmony. Unanimity replaces critical thinking.

discovery.text: Warning signs: an illusion of invulnerability, pressure on dissenters, self-censorship, and shared stereotyping.

twist.text: After Bay of Pigs, JFK restructured meetings. He assigned a devil's advocate and left the room to reduce conformity.

climax.text: In important group decisions, appoint someone to argue against the consensus. Dissent is a feature, not a bug.

punchline.text: When everyone agrees too fast, nobody is thinking.

quiz.question: What did JFK do after the Bay of Pigs to prevent groupthink?
options: Assigned a devil's advocate and left the room during discussions
